correctness.rationale: Every chart generator is represented in a Laurent lattice. By the Ferrers inequalities its primitive generators split into an SW Ferrers semigroup, a disjoint NE Ferrers semigroup and 2(m+1-i-j) free variables. The remaining edge ratios factor into those generators; the supports are disjoint, proving an algebraic tensor-product isomorphism. Since factors are standard graded, their Hilbert series give exactly the local Hilbert–Samuel series. Corso–Nagel Example 5.11 yields Narayana numerators for the transposed local partitions, and their values at 1 are Catalan; primitive-generator count gives tangent dimensions, while Catalan supermultiplicativity gives the extremal criterion. 285 exact finite chart checks and bounded semigroup enumerations corroborate but do not replace this infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Corso–Nagel supplies global Hilbert functions for Ferrers rings and Gonciulea–Lakshmibai supplies singular-component geometry of broader ladder varieties. Neither of those premises by itself identifies every staircase toric fixed-point chart as an explicit three-factor product, nor yields all pointwise Hilbert–Samuel series. Matched statements, transposed shapes and stronger singularity-coverage results were compared; relevant primary full text inspected, with specified residual broad-literature risk.

value.rationale: The theorem determines local algebraic germs and full Hilbert–Samuel series at all fixed points in a natural infinite family of projective toric varieties. The exact Catalan products identify a four-point smoothness locus among torus fixed points and unique exponentially singular corners. These are meaningful local geometric invariants, more informative than simply recalling a global Ferrers degree formula, and are natural input to singular-stratum and resolution investigations.
